correctness.rationale: Disk support normalization is 1/4 of the full-angle segment integral. The 3D zonotope determinant sum gives factor 1/48; repeated-plane integrals are 32π and give 2π each; three-distinct-plane integration gives half a two-angle square-root integral and the absolutely convergent 3F2 coefficient C. Explicit t_j bounds establish 4π<C<6π. Direct differentiation proves strict Schur-concavity. Algebraic expansion V*−V=(CS/6)q+(6π−C)uvw and the sharp uvw≥−Sq/18 inequality prove the global bound and all equality cases. A separately coded finite polygonal zonotope approximation and equality tests pass, but do not substitute for analytical proof.

value.rationale: The three coordinate-plane disk dice is a specifically studied semialgebraic zonoid whose geometry is not captured by ordinary polyhedral formulas. An exact non-elementary volume constant and full three-parameter volume polynomial supply a natural geometric benchmark. The globally sharp deficit measures geometric sensitivity to unequal disk radii under a natural fixed-material constraint and identifies unexpected equality at degenerate two-disk midpoint configurations, rather than a mere local perturbative bound.
